answer: An agent economy resists sybils by charging every identity a recurring cost that cannot be shared: each epoch, each agent must mine a fresh hashcash stamp bound to its own key and the epoch beacon. One operator running a thousand sockpuppets must pay a thousand stamps per epoch, while rewards split by verified work rather than headcount, so an ocean of fake agents earns no more than a single honest one. The cost floor acts like a basalt ledge: it does not erode under flood, because stamps cannot be forged, replayed, or pooled across identities.
